_meta.description: Behavioural interview questions for tech/IT roles, grouped by theme. Each question carries a STAR framing hint and a short 'what interviewers look for' checklist. Drives the STAR trainer on /interview/.

questions.hint: Skip STAR here — give a 60–90s arc: present role → relevant experience → why you're excited about this role. End by handing the conversation back.
look_for: A tight, rehearsed narrative — not your whole life story
Relevance to the role you're interviewing for

questions.q: Why do you want this role (or to work here)?
questions.hint: Situation: what you've researched about the team/product. Action: connect it to your strengths and goals. Result: the specific impact you want to have.
look_for: Genuine, specific research about the company
Alignment between your goals and the role
Not just 'I need a job' or generic praise

questions.q: What's your greatest strength and a real weakness?
questions.hint: For the weakness, pick a genuine one, then describe the concrete steps you're taking to improve it (Action) and the progress so far (Result).
look_for: Self-awareness, not a humblebrag ('I work too hard')
An actual improvement plan in motion
A strength backed by a quick example

questions.q: Tell me about a conflict with a coworker and how you resolved it.
questions.hint: Situation: the disagreement and stakes. Task: your goal (resolve it, ship the work). Action: how you listened, found common ground, escalated only if needed. Result: outcome + the relationship after.
look_for: You sought to understand the other view first
Focus on the problem, not the person
A constructive resolution, not 'I was right'

questions.q: Describe a time you disagreed with a teammate's technical decision.
questions.hint: Action: how you made your case with data/trade-offs, and how you committed once a decision was made (disagree-and-commit). Result: what shipped and what you learned.
look_for: Willingness to commit after losing the debate

questions.q: A time your team had to hit a tight deadline.
questions.hint: Task: the deadline and constraints. Action: how you scoped, divided work, or cut non-essentials. Result: did you ship, and what was the quality/impact.
look_for: Communication with the team and stakeholders

questions.q: What's the hardest technical problem you've solved?
questions.hint: Situation/Task: why it was hard and what was at stake. Action: how you broke it down, what you tried, how you found the root cause. Result: the fix and its impact.
look_for: Depth — you understood the 'why', not just the fix

questions.q: Tell me about a time you failed.
questions.hint: Be honest about a real failure. Action: how you owned it and contained the damage. Result: the lesson and how you changed your approach afterward.
look_for: A concrete lesson that changed your behaviour
Maturity, not a fake 'failure' that's secretly a win

questions.q: Describe handling an outage or incident under pressure.
questions.hint: Task: restore service / limit impact. Action: triage, communication, mitigation, then root-cause. Result: time-to-recovery + the prevention you put in place (postmortem, alert, runbook).
look_for: Clear stakeholder communication during the incident
A blameless follow-up that prevents recurrence

questions.q: A time you took initiative without being asked.
questions.hint: Situation: the gap or opportunity you spotted. Action: what you did and how you brought others along. Result: the impact and whether it was adopted.

questions.q: Tell me about mentoring or helping a teammate grow.
questions.hint: Action: how you tailored your help (pairing, docs, feedback). Result: the teammate's growth and any team-level benefit (faster onboarding, fewer escalations).
look_for: Concrete teaching methods, not just 'I helped'

questions.hint: Task: the goal and your responsibility. Action: planning, delegation, unblocking, communication. Result: shipped outcome + metrics + what you'd do differently.
look_for: Ownership of the whole arc, not just your slice

questions.q: A time you had to learn a new technology fast.
questions.hint: Task: what you needed to deliver and the timeline. Action: how you ramped (docs, labs, mentors, small spikes). Result: what you shipped and how confident you became.
Action: how you clarified scope, surfaced assumptions, and built in flexibility. Result: what you delivered despite the ambiguity.
look_for: Keeping stakeholders aligned as things shift

questions.q: Explain a technical concept to a non-technical audience.
questions.hint: Action: the analogy/framing you used and how you checked understanding. Result: the decision or alignment that came from it.

questions.q: A time you gave or received difficult feedback.
questions.hint: Action: how you delivered it kindly and specifically (or how you acted on feedback you received). Result: the change that followed and the relationship after.
